newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Paraibuna sets new zinc record in March.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Paraibuna sets new zinc record in March.

text.p: Paraibuna Metais, part of Brazil's Paranapanema Group produced a record 6,128 tonnes of molten zinc in March, the firm said Thursday.
The previous mark of 6,088 tonnes was set in July 1996.
According to Paraibuna director Antonio Miguel Marques, last month's result was due to new operational procedures which were introduced at the beginning of 1997.
Zinc purity which was at 97 percent in 1996 reached 97.5 percent last month and copper purity rose to 83.9 percent from 71.5 percent.
Paraibuna's zinc output is expected to reach 75,000 tonnes in 1997, up from 65,000 tonnes in 1996.
Work is also moving quickly on the construction of the Sobragi hydro-electric plant which involves an investment of $50 million but which will result in a sharp reduction in power costs, it said.
"Electric power is the main input for Paraibuna after zinc concentrate and represents a cost of $150 a tonne produced," Marques said.

"With Sobragi this cost will be reduced to $20, which will represent a saving of $1 million in outgoings and the guarantee of supply at a time when many specialists are warning the system will be overloaded," he added.
The plant will be generating power in July 1998 and should be fully operational in December of that year.
